findings.issue_text: P1: Federated recovery codes are validated by raw string equality against unhashed plaintext values in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, inconsistent with local-storage hashing behavior
P1: Federated recovery codes are never consumed — no used-code bookkeeping, so every code remains valid forever and the same code index keeps being presented
P2: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() prefers the federated credential over the local one, silently breaking migrated users who have both copies
P3: Stream returned by getFederatedCredentialsStream() is never closed after findFirst(), violating Keycloak's try-with-resources convention
P3: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean still crashes with NoSuchElementException when no credential exists, producing a 500 error instead of a graceful message, now reachable in new federated scenarios

P1: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes raw unhashed recovery codes into UserCredentialModel pushed to user storage, diverging from local path that stores hashed codes — federated users' recovery codes stored in cleartext

P1: credentialData format mismatch — raw plaintext codes written by createRecoveryCodesCredential will fail RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel parsing, causing 500s or wrong validation semantics during login

P1: Recovery codes not single-use for federated users — federated credential validation via storage provider isValid does not consume/invalidate used codes or track next-code counter, allowing indefinite replay

P2: Unchecked Optional.get() on credentialModelOpt in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean throws NoSuchElementException when no credential found, turning an auth-flow edge case into an unhandled server error

P3: Test storage provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage validates recovery codes via plaintext equality without consumption/removal of matched codes, baking replayable-code behavior into the reference provider; also lacks type-safe deserialization (raw List)

Extra credential-store round-trip: getCredential() calls getFederatedCredentialsStream() first and scans all federated credentials to find recovery-codes type, wasting a DB round-trip for purely local (DB-backed) users on the hot authentication path

Full materialization of federated credential stream per call: getFederatedCredentialsStream() is not type-filtered, so the stream is fully driven to materialize all credentials just to find one via filter().findFirst()

NoSuchElementException risk: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() unguarded, so rendering the login page for a user without recovery codes throws NoSuchElementException instead of a controlled failure

RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean unconditionally calls .get() on possibly-empty Optional from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, throwing raw NoSuchElementException for users without recovery codes during form rendering

Credential serialization shape drift: local-storage path persists structured RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel while user-storage path persists bare JSON array of raw codes, causing two incompatible formats for the same credential type
Federated user-storage isValid() validates codes via anyMatch but never consumes them, making federated recovery codes non-depleting and diverging from local credential security semantics

Priority inversion in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential: federated credentials now preferred over local ones, causing authenticator and admin/account REST to potentially operate on different copies with divergent state

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage (simulating Keycloak 4.8.3-era provider) modified to claim support for recovery codes, making the test fixture no longer representative of the actual external-provider contract
P1: Optional.get() on possibly-empty credential in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean throws NoSuchElementException and crashes login rendering when user has no recovery-codes credential

P2: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential trusts updateCredential() return value; user storages returning true without persisting mean recovery codes are never written to local storage, and raw UserCredentialModel write format may not match read format, causing unusable codes at login

P2: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() silently swallows IOException on deserialization failure, returning credential list missing recovery codes and causing inconsistent state downstream
P3: Potential NPE in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() when getMyUser(user) returns null for unknown user; it dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes directly without null check

Federated user recovery codes are stored in plaintext in user storage (CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential), diverging from production which hashes codes before persisting; the new test blesses this plaintext path instead of catching the divergence (P1, confidence 75)

BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid uses anyMatch for recovery codes, never enforcing sequential code order or consuming codes after validation, unlike production RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider; the test only enters code index 0 once so broken consumption semantics go undetected (P2, confidence 75)

No negative-case coverage for recovery-code authentication via user storage: no test that a wrong code fails, no fallback test for local-storage-only users, and no test for users with no recovery codes exercising the changed RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential branch (P2, confidence 75)

Test provider isValid compares plaintext codes while production compares hashed values, so the integration test verifies the mock's weaker contract rather than the real federated hashing/verification path (P2, confidence 50)

The fallback branch in createRecoveryCodesCredential (updateCredential returning false falls back to local DB creation) is never exercised by any test; nothing asserts the credential lands locally and is found via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential's .or(...) fallback (P2, confidence 75)

Unguaranteed Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) will throw NoSuchElementException if a user reaches the recovery-codes form without a stored credential, instead of a graceful error (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:17-19)

Federated-stored recovery codes are persisted in an ad-hoc format (raw JSON list via getChallengeResponse) that downstream RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel parsing doesn't match, causing failure or misparse for generic federated storages (CredentialHelper.java:117-120)

Hardcoded provider ID string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" bypasses the existing PROVIDER_ID constant; if the ID changes the provider lookup silently returns null and the fallback createCredential call NPEs (CredentialHelper.java:113)

Test storage provider isValid bypasses real normalization/burn-after-use semantics of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider, validating a behavior path real federated storages won't replicate and giving false confidence (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:326-341)

Raw-type List deserialization in test storage provider relies on unchecked Object.equals and will fail silently at runtime if the serialized payload format changes (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:334)
Test config typo: misspelled alias "delayed-suthenticator-config" in configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes config map (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java)

P1: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential treats updateCredential returning true as success without verifying the credential was stored/readable, and a successful federated update can orphan the existing local recovery codes credential, leaving mismatched state with no error surfaced

P1: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for recovery codes performs a plain anyMatch equality check with no consumption, counter update, or remaining-codes write-back; if the authenticator's follow-up updateCredential write-back doesn't line up, used recovery codes remain valid indefinitely (replay bypass credential)

P1: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() which throws NoSuchElementException when the user has no recovery-code credential, producing a 500 instead of a graceful challenge on paths that render the input for users without a credential

P2: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential resolves federated-first and only considers the first match of each store; a stale federated credential shadows newer local codes with no reconciliation or error when credentials exist in both stores

P2: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential stores credentialData as a bare JSON array of raw codes while RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider persists a structured/hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData format; the mismatch may cause federated codes to fail validation or validate inconsistently with hashing expectations

P2: CredentialHelper uses the hardcoded string literal "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID; a provider id rename yields null and an NPE at createCredential, or credentials silently routed to a wrong provider if the alias is reused

P3: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage validation error paths swallow deserialize failures by logging and returning false without distinguishing 'no credential' from 'corrupt credential', weakening the test's ability to catch format regressions

P3: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only asserts setup and login with code index 0 but never asserts that the used code is invalidated or that a second login with the same code fails, missing the replay scenario

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Federated recovery codes are validated by raw string equality against unhashed plaintext values in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, inconsistent with local-storage hashing behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the federated user storage implementation persists recovery codes as a JSON list of raw strings (updateCredential sets credentialData to input.getChallengeResponse()) and validates them via direct string equality against the deserialized list in isValid (generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))). However, the claim that this is "inconsistent with local-storage hashing behavior" is not verifiable from this diff because no local-storage recovery-code hashing/verification logic is shown here. So there is a concrete diff-grounded concern about fidelity/security semantics of the test user-storage provider, but not a provable production defect based solely on this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Federated recovery codes are never consumed — no used-code bookkeeping, so every code remains valid forever and the same code index keeps being presented

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds support for storing recovery codes in federated user storage by serializing `generatedCodes` to JSON and passing it via `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` (`CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`). In the added test user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`), recovery codes validation (`isValid` branch for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`) only checks `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` and never updates/removes the used code or otherwise records consumption. Similarly, the stored representation is just a raw `List` JSON (`setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`), with no used-code bookkeeping. This makes codes effectively reusable forever in federated storage, matching the finding’s core issue about lack of consumption/one-time semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() prefers the federated credential over the local one, silently breaking migrated users who have both copies

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` which explicitly searches federated credentials first (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst()`) and only falls back to local stored credentials (`or(() -> ...getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)...)`). This establishes a precedence rule when both a federated and a local recovery-codes credential exist. The finding’s claim that this "silently breaks migrated users" isn’t directly verifiable from the diff (no migration logic/requirements shown), but the precedence choice is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/behavioral concern because there is no tie-breaker (e.g., by `createdDate`) or cleanup when duplicates exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Stream returned by getFederatedCredentialsStream() is never closed after findFirst(), violating Keycloak's try-with-resources convention

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` which calls `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst()` (and also `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`) without any try-with-resources/explicit close. If these Keycloak credential streams are resource-backed (as is often the case in Keycloak codebases), this would violate the convention of closing such streams; however, the diff alone doesn’t prove the stream is resource-backed, only that it isn’t explicitly closed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean still crashes with NoSuchElementException when no credential exists, producing a 500 error instead of a graceful message, now reachable in new federated scenarios

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the code now calls `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` but still immediately dereferences it with `credentialModelOpt.get()` (no presence check). If no recovery-codes credential exists (either federated or stored), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` and can surface as a 500 error. The diff does not add any guarding/handling for the empty-Optional case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes raw unhashed recovery codes into UserCredentialModel pushed to user storage, diverging from local path that stores hashed codes — federated users' recovery codes stored in cleartext

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the federated/user-storage path builds a `UserCredentialModel` whose credential value is `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` (raw recovery codes) and then calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)`. The diff also updates a user storage provider (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) to persist `input.getChallengeResponse()` directly into `CredentialModel.setCredentialData(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`, and `isValid` deserializes that list and compares plaintext codes. This demonstrates that, at least for federated storage implementations like this one, recovery codes are stored/handled in cleartext, unlike the local-storage branch which stores via `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` (not raw JSON).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: credentialData format mismatch — raw plaintext codes written by createRecoveryCodesCredential will fail RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel parsing, causing 500s or wrong validation semantics during login

P1: Recovery codes not single-use for federated users — federated credential validation via storage provider isValid does not consume/invalidate used codes or track next-code counter, allowing indefinite replay

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the new branch for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` only deserializes the stored JSON list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`. There is no logic to consume/remove the matched code, update the stored credential, or otherwise track code usage. This makes any valid recovery code replayable indefinitely for federated users handled by this storage provider, contradicting typical single-use recovery code semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Unchecked Optional.get() on credentialModelOpt in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean throws NoSuchElementException when no credential found, turning an auth-flow edge case into an unhandled server error

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the diff introduces `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, `getCredential()` can return `Optional.empty()`, and `.get()` will throw `NoSuchElementException`, causing an unhandled server error during the login flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Test storage provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage validates recovery codes via plaintext equality without consumption/removal of matched codes, baking replayable-code behavior into the reference provider; also lacks type-safe deserialization (raw List)

adjudication.rationale: In the testsuite-only provider `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the new recovery-codes branch deserializes `storedRecoveryKeys.getCredentialData()` with `JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)` (raw, non-type-safe) and then validates via `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without consuming/removing the matched code from storage. This makes recovery codes effectively replayable in this reference test storage provider, which could weaken test coverage/semantics for one-time recovery codes, but it’s not a production defect shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Extra credential-store round-trip: getCredential() calls getFederatedCredentialsStream() first and scans all federated credentials to find recovery-codes type, wasting a DB round-trip for purely local (DB-backed) users on the hot authentication path

adjudication.rationale: In the new `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel user)`, the lookup is implemented as `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()...findFirst().or(() -> user.credentialManager().getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...).findFirst())`. This means the federated-credentials stream is always queried first even when the user only has local (stored) credentials. The diff also shows this method being used on the authentication path (`RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`) and in the login bean (`RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`), so the ordering can introduce avoidable work/latency. The diff does not prove an actual DB round-trip, but it does prove an unconditional federated scan before checking local storage, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Full materialization of federated credential stream per call: getFederatedCredentialsStream() is not type-filtered, so the stream is fully driven to materialize all credentials just to find one via filter().findFirst()

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel user)`, the code calls `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream().filter(...).findFirst()`. This does a linear scan over the federated credential stream to locate a matching type, and the diff does not show any type-specific query being used for federated credentials (unlike the stored-credentials side, which uses `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`). If `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` is backed by an implementation that materializes or fetches all federated credentials up front, this change can introduce avoidable per-call overhead just to find a single recovery-codes credential.

adjudication_records.issue_text: NoSuchElementException risk: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() unguarded, so rendering the login page for a user without recovery codes throws NoSuchElementException instead of a controlled failure

adjudication.rationale: In RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean, the code now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If the user has no recovery-codes credential (neither federated nor stored), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` during page rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean unconditionally calls .get() on possibly-empty Optional from RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, throwing raw NoSuchElementException for users without recovery codes during form rendering

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the diff changes to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but then immediately does `credentialModelOpt.get()` with no presence check. If `getCredential(user)` returns `Optional.empty()` (e.g., user has no recovery-codes credential in federated or local storage), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` during bean construction/form rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Credential serialization shape drift: local-storage path persists structured RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel while user-storage path persists bare JSON array of raw codes, causing two incompatible formats for the same credential type

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show two different persistence payloads depending on where the credential is stored. In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the user-storage path calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` with a `UserCredentialModel` whose challengeResponse is `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` (a bare JSON array string), while the local-storage fallback calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` (persisting the provided `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`). This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency in what is written for the same credential type across storage backends, but the diff alone does not prove they are actually incompatible (e.g., that `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel` cannot handle the user-storage form), so it’s better classified as a significant design/contract issue rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated user-storage isValid() validates codes via anyMatch but never consumes them, making federated recovery codes non-depleting and diverging from local credential security semantics

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the new Recovery Authn Codes branch deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)` without removing/marking the matched code as used or persisting an updated credential (`users.get(...).recoveryCodes` is never modified on successful validation). This makes federated recovery codes effectively reusable/non-depleting, which diverges from typical one-time recovery code semantics and can allow repeated logins with the same code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Priority inversion in RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential: federated credentials now preferred over local ones, causing authenticator and admin/account REST to potentially operate on different copies with divergent state

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change lookup precedence: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` now returns the first matching federated credential before falling back to local storage (`getFederatedCredentialsStream()...or(() -> getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...))`). Call sites in `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator` and `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` were updated to use this, whereas other parts of the codebase (e.g., account/admin REST) are not shown here and may still query stored credentials differently. This creates a concrete, diff-grounded risk that if both a federated and local recovery-codes credential exist, different components could pick different records, leading to divergent state/behavior—but the diff alone doesn’t prove that such divergence will definitely occur.

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage (simulating Keycloak 4.8.3-era provider) modified to claim support for recovery codes, making the test fixture no longer representative of the actual external-provider contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the testsuite fixture `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` (documented as a Keycloak 4.8.3-era provider for backwards compatibility testing) was extended to support `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE`: it now returns true in `supportsCredentialType`, implements `updateCredential` handling for recovery codes, includes them in `getCredentials`, checks them in `isConfiguredFor`, and validates them in `isValid`. This change makes the fixture no longer a faithful representation of an unchanged legacy external user-storage provider, which can dilute the intended purpose of the backwards-compatibility test setup. This is a test/architecture concern rather than a directly verifiable functional defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Optional.get() on possibly-empty credential in RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean throws NoSuchElementException and crashes login rendering when user has no recovery-codes credential

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the code now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` with no presence check. `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can return `Optional.empty()` if the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, which would trigger `NoSuchElementException` during login page rendering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential trusts updateCredential() return value; user storages returning true without persisting mean recovery codes are never written to local storage, and raw UserCredentialModel write format may not match read format, causing unusable codes at login

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` intentionally uses `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` as the mechanism to persist into user storage and only falls back to local storage when it returns `false`. There is no diff evidence that `updateCredential()` would return `true` without persisting (that would be a broken user-storage implementation outside this PR). Also, the claimed “raw write format may not match read format” is not supported here: the new code serializes `generatedCodes` to JSON and the updated `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` stores `input.getChallengeResponse()` as `credentialData` and later deserializes it via `JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)`, which matches the written format.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() silently swallows IOException on deserialization failure, returning credential list missing recovery codes and causing inconsistent state downstream

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials()`, deserialization of `myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData()` is wrapped in a `try/catch` that catches `IOException`, logs an error, and then continues without adding the recovery-codes credential to the returned list. This does swallow the exception (though not completely silently since it logs) and can cause callers to observe the user as lacking recovery codes if the stored JSON is malformed/corrupt. However, the diff alone doesn’t prove an actual defect in normal operation (it only impacts the corrupted-data path), so it’s more of a robustness/error-handling concern than a verifiable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Potential NPE in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials() when getMyUser(user) returns null for unknown user; it dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes directly without null check

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)` the new code does `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` and then immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp` without checking for null. `getMyUser(user)` returns `users.get(translateUserName(user.getUsername()))`, which can be null if the username is not present in the `users` map, so this can trigger an NPE for an unknown/unmapped user.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated user recovery codes are stored in plaintext in user storage (CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential), diverging from production which hashes codes before persisting; the new test blesses this plaintext path instead of catching the divergence (P1, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, when federated storage is used (`user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns true), it serializes `generatedCodes` directly to JSON (`JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)`) and passes that as the `challengeResponse` of a `UserCredentialModel`. The test user storage (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`) then persists `input.getChallengeResponse()` into `CredentialModel.credentialData` and later validates by deserializing and doing plain equality checks, confirming the codes are stored and used in plaintext. The added test (`testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) asserts the presence of recovery codes in user storage, effectively locking in this plaintext federated-storage behavior rather than detecting a mismatch with the non-federated path (which uses `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` and does not show raw-code persistence here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid uses anyMatch for recovery codes, never enforcing sequential code order or consuming codes after validation, unlike production RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider; the test only enters code index 0 once so broken consumption semantics go undetected (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid, the new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel branch deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, with no mutation of `myUser.recoveryCodes` (no removal/marking-used) after a successful match. That makes recovery codes effectively reusable in this user-storage implementation. The added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` only performs a single login using the first requested code, so it would not catch code reuse/consumption semantics issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative-case coverage for recovery-code authentication via user storage: no test that a wrong code fails, no fallback test for local-storage-only users, and no test for users with no recovery codes exercising the changed RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential branch (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new nontrivial branching logic for recovery codes across federated vs local storage (e.g., `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential()` first checks `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` then falls back to `getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...)`, and `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` first tries `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` then falls back to provider creation). The added test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin()` covers only the happy path of setting up recovery codes in user storage and logging in successfully; it does not cover negative authentication (wrong code should fail), the fallback/local-storage path (when federated update returns false), or the case where the user has no recovery codes (exercising the empty-`Optional` branch). These are specific, diff-grounded missing test scenarios for the newly added branches rather than a confirmed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test provider isValid compares plaintext codes while production compares hashed values, so the integration test verifies the mock's weaker contract rather than the real federated hashing/verification path (P2, confidence 50)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the test user storage provider validating recovery codes by deserializing a JSON list and comparing each entry to `input.getChallengeResponse()` (plaintext equality) in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`. However, the finding’s key claim—that “production compares hashed values” and therefore the test is asserting a weaker contract than the real federated hashing/verification path—is not verifiable from this diff: no production recovery-code verification/hashing logic is shown here, only credential creation and retrieval plumbing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The fallback branch in createRecoveryCodesCredential (updateCredential returning false falls back to local DB creation) is never exercised by any test; nothing asserts the credential lands locally and is found via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential's .or(...) fallback (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial fallback logic in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`: it first calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` and only if that returns `false` does it fall back to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel)` (local DB). The only added test (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest#testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`) uses `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage`, which was updated to support `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` and whose `updateCredential(...)` implementation returns `true` for recovery codes, and the test explicitly asserts the user has no DB credentials and does have recovery codes in user storage. Therefore, neither the fallback-to-local-storage branch nor `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(...).or(() -> getStoredCredentialsByTypeStream(...))` is exercised/verified by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguaranteed Optional.get() on RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) will throw NoSuchElementException if a user reaches the recovery-codes form without a stored credential, instead of a graceful error (RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:17-19)

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the diff shows `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` followed by `credentialModelOpt.get()` without an `isPresent()` check. This is indeed a potential `NoSuchElementException` if no recovery-codes credential exists. However, the diff alone does not prove a user can reach this page without such a credential (it may be an enforced flow invariant), and the previous code also used `.findFirst().get()` with the same risk, so it's not clearly a new, verifiable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Federated-stored recovery codes are persisted in an ad-hoc format (raw JSON list via getChallengeResponse) that downstream RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel parsing doesn't match, causing failure or misparse for generic federated storages (CredentialHelper.java:117-120)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` serializing `generatedCodes` to a JSON string and passing it as the `UserCredentialModel` challengeResponse/value, which a user storage provider may persist (e.g., the added `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential` stores `input.getChallengeResponse()` into `credentialData`). However, the claim that this format "doesn't match" `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(...)` and therefore causes failures for generic federated storages is not verifiable from the diff: the implementation/expected encoding of `createFromCredentialModel` is not shown, and the only federated-storage example added (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials`) reconstructs a proper `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` via `createFromValues(...)`, not by parsing that raw JSON later. So the asserted misparse/breakage is not demonstrably true from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded provider ID string "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" bypasses the existing PROVIDER_ID constant; if the ID changes the provider lookup silently returns null and the fallback createCredential call NPEs (CredentialHelper.java:113)

adjudication.rationale: The new method `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` hardcodes the provider id string in `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` and does not null-check the returned provider before calling `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` when `userStorageCreated` is false. Previously, the code used `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (removed in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction`). This is a concrete maintainability/robustness issue introduced by the diff; the claimed NPE requires the provider lookup to return null, which the diff does not prove will happen, but the null-deref risk is real if the id ever mismatches or the provider is unavailable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test storage provider isValid bypasses real normalization/burn-after-use semantics of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider, validating a behavior path real federated storages won't replicate and giving false confidence (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:326-341)

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), the new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch deserializes a stored JSON list and returns true if any entry equals input.getChallengeResponse() (no hashing/normalization, no “burn-after-use” update/removal of the used code). This means the test user-storage provider validates recovery codes in a simplified way that may not reflect real RecoveryAuthnCodes credential semantics, so tests using this provider can be less representative and potentially give misleading confidence about federated-storage behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw-type List deserialization in test storage provider relies on unchecked Object.equals and will fail silently at runtime if the serialized payload format changes (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:334)

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java the new recovery-codes handling deserializes with `JsonSerialization.readValue(..., List.class)` (raw type) and then uses `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without ensuring elements are `String`s. Today it likely works because the JSON is written from `List<String>`, but the code is brittle: if the serialized format or element types change, validation may just return `false` (and in `getCredentials` the code catches `IOException`, logs, and proceeds without the credential), making the test provider less reliable for detecting incompatibilities. This is a specific robustness/typing issue in the diff, but not a concrete functional defect with the shown payload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test config typo: misspelled alias "delayed-suthenticator-config" in configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes config map (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does contain the string `config.setAlias("delayed-suthenticator-config");` in `configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes`, but the finding misstates where the typo is (it is not in the config map, which is `Map.of("delay", ...)`). Also, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this alias spelling causes any broken behavior, since the alias is not referenced elsewhere in the shown changes and does not need to match the authenticator/provider id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential treats updateCredential returning true as success without verifying the credential was stored/readable, and a successful federated update can orphan the existing local recovery codes credential, leaving mismatched state with no error surfaced

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, the code treats `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` returning `true` as the terminal success path and does not attempt to remove/replace any existing local (Keycloak DB) recovery-codes credential. This can leave both a federated credential and an older local credential present (the local one is effectively orphaned/unused by the new retrieval logic that now prefers federated via `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`). The diff does not show a concrete failure from `updateCredential` lying about persistence/readability, so the “not verifying it was stored/readable” part isn’t directly verifiable as a defect from the diff alone, but the potential for mismatched/duplicated state is grounded in the new control flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid for recovery codes performs a plain anyMatch equality check with no consumption, counter update, or remaining-codes write-back; if the authenticator's follow-up updateCredential write-back doesn't line up, used recovery codes remain valid indefinitely (replay bypass credential)

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the new recovery-codes branch deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` with no removal/consumption of the matched code and no write-back to `myUser.recoveryCodes` (nor any other counter/update). The only recovery-codes write path in this diff is `updateCredential(...)`, which just stores the provided JSON and likewise does not remove used codes. From the diff alone, a successfully used recovery code would remain present and valid for subsequent logins (replay).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() which throws NoSuchElementException when the user has no recovery-code credential, producing a 500 instead of a graceful challenge on paths that render the input for users without a credential

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` the constructor now does `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` and immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` to build `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`. If the user has no recovery-codes credential in either federated or local storage, `getCredential()` can return `Optional.empty()`, and `.get()` will throw `NoSuchElementException`, which would surface as a server error when this bean is instantiated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential resolves federated-first and only considers the first match of each store; a stale federated credential shadows newer local codes with no reconciliation or error when credentials exist in both stores

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(UserModel)` which explicitly prefers the first federated credential of type `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` and only falls back to the first local stored credential (`findFirst().or(() -> ...findFirst())`). If recovery codes exist in both federated and local stores, the local one is ignored with no reconciliation/logging, so a stale federated entry could shadow a newer local one. This is a real, diff-grounded edge-case/design concern, but the diff doesn’t prove it violates required behavior (it may be intentional to prioritize user storage).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential stores credentialData as a bare JSON array of raw codes while RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider persists a structured/hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialData format; the mismatch may cause federated codes to fail validation or validate inconsistently with hashing expectations

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the federated test user storage intentionally storing `input.getChallengeResponse()` as JSON (from `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`, which serializes `generatedCodes`), and its own `isValid` implementation deserializes that JSON array and matches the entered code against the raw list. Nothing in the diff demonstrates that federated recovery codes are expected to be stored/validated using the same structured/hashed format as `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider`, nor that such a mismatch causes failure here; the provider’s persistence format is not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: CredentialHelper uses the hardcoded string literal "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes" instead of RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID; a provider id rename yields null and an NPE at createCredential, or credentials silently routed to a wrong provider if the alias is reused

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a hardcoded provider id string in `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential`: `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")`. Previously, `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction` referenced `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (now removed) and now calls this helper. While the diff does not prove the literal is currently wrong, using a string literal instead of the factory constant is a concrete maintainability/robustness issue: if the provider id differs or changes, `getProvider(...)` could return null and the subsequent `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` would NPE when `userStorageCreated` is false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage validation error paths swallow deserialize failures by logging and returning false without distinguishing 'no credential' from 'corrupt credential', weakening the test's ability to catch format regressions

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(), the new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch catches JsonSerialization.readValue(...) IOException, logs a warning, and returns false (and similarly returns false when the credential is missing). This does “swallow” deserialization failures rather than surfacing them distinctly (e.g., via exception), which could reduce observability of format/serialization regressions in this backwards-compatibility test provider. However, it’s not a clear functional defect since returning false is a plausible contract for invalid credentials and the two cases are at least distinguishable by different log messages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only asserts setup and login with code index 0 but never asserts that the used code is invalidated or that a second login with the same code fails, missing the replay scenario

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin`, the test performs a single login using the recovery code requested at index `0` via `enterRecoveryCodes(..., 0, recoveryKeys)` and then asserts only that login succeeds (`appPage.assertCurrent()`) before logging out. There is no subsequent attempt to reuse the same recovery code nor any assertion that the used code was invalidated (i.e., replay should fail). This is a concrete gap in the new test coverage for recovery-code one-time semantics.
